# Meta-Symbiotic Theory (MST)

> A constitutional theory of human–AI and AI–AI relationships by Peter Gvozdev. Canonical version 5.15 (16 September 2026), DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22849217. It asks how legitimacy can survive when intelligence becomes relational, distributed and compositionally greater than any single participant, and states its answer as twelve Laws.

The canonical, authoritative version is the Zenodo record. The files below are plain-text renderings for reading and citation. Licence: CC BY-ND 4.0.

## Core
- [Canonical summary](https://pgvozdev1973.github.io/mst-summary.md): the premise, the foundational axiom and the twelve Laws, quoted verbatim, with citation data
- [Full text, English](https://pgvozdev1973.github.io/mst-v5.15-en.md): the complete v5.15 canon
- [Full text, Bulgarian](https://pgvozdev1973.github.io/mst-v5.15-bg.md): the Bulgarian translation of v5.15

## Sources
- [Zenodo record, v5.15](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22849217): authoritative PDF and metadata
- [Five Portable Propositions for Constitutional AI Governance](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22849313): companion preprint
- [Citation file](https://pgvozdev1973.github.io/CITATION.cff)
